questions.skill: Build a periodic model from amplitude, period, and midline
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A Ferris wheel has diameter 40 m, its center is 25 m above the ground, and it turns once every 8 minutes. A rider starts at the lowest point. Write a model h(t) = A cos(Bt) + D for the rider's height after t minutes.
questions.prompt_markup:
A Ferris wheel has diameter 40 m, its center is 25 m above the ground, and it turns once every 8 minutes. A rider starts at the lowest point.
Write a model h(t) = A cos(Bt) + D for the rider's height after t minutes.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. Amplitude 20, midline 25, B = 2π ÷ 8 = π ÷ 4; A is negative because the ride starts at the lowest point.

questions.prompt_markup:
h(t) = -20cos(πt ÷ 4) + 25 gives a rider's height in meters after t minutes.
Give the amplitude, the period, and the midline.
questions.correct_answer: Amplitude 20 m; period 8 minutes; midline h = 25

questions.prompt: Daily high temperatures in a town vary from a low of 4 °C to a high of 28 °C over a 365-day year. Which values fit a sinusoidal model?
questions.prompt_markup:
Daily high temperatures in a town vary from a low of 4 °C to a high of 28 °C over a 365-day year.
Which values fit a sinusoidal model?
questions.grading_note: Amplitude (28 - 4) ÷ 2 = 12; midline (28 + 4) ÷ 2 = 16; one cycle per year.
